back: Agreement (no two nodes decide differently), validity (the value was proposed by someone), termination (live nodes eventually decide).
Same start state + same commands in the same order = same end state on every node. Consensus agrees on the order.

front: What does FLP say, and how do Raft and Paxos live with it?
back: No deterministic algorithm guarantees termination in a fully asynchronous network with one crash. They never compromise safety and use timeouts for progress.
Follower (passive), candidate (asking for votes), leader (takes all writes, at most one per term).
See a higher term: adopt it and become a follower. See a request with a lower term: reject it.
So one follower usually times out first and wins, avoiding repeated split votes. The paper's example range is 150–300 ms.
At most one, first come first served, and only to a candidate whose log is at least as up to date.

front: When is a Raft entry committed?
back: When the leader has stored an entry from its current term on a majority of nodes (leader included).

front: Commit latency of a 5-node Raft cluster?
back: Roughly the second-fastest follower's round trip plus a disk sync. Slow followers don't count.

front: What does a follower check on every append?
back: That it has an entry matching the previous index and term. If not, it rejects and the leader backs up until logs match.
Vote only for candidates whose last entry has a higher term, or the same term and an equal or higher index. Guarantees new leaders have every committed entry.

front: Why can't a Raft leader serve reads from memory alone?
back: It may have been deposed without knowing. Confirm leadership with a majority first (ReadIndex) or use a clock-bounded lease.
Prepare/promise (reserve proposal number n, learn prior accepted values), then accept/accepted (a majority accepts a value).
etcd: Raft, keys with leases, watches, compare-and-swap. ZooKeeper: Zab, ephemeral and sequential znodes, watches.

front: What belongs in a coordination service?
back: Small facts that must be unambiguous: leader, locks, shard map, config. Not bulk data.
